findings.source_passage: Whether wanted or not, murals adorned the sides of the buildings and the streetlight posts. Trees were randomly planted in holes that littered the sidewalks. Signs outside the bottom floors of apartment buildings advertised everything from palm reading to palm trees.
findings.source_locator: paragraph describing the arts district, before Miriam reaches Heather's building
findings.why_it_matters: The source's wry, specific neighborhood description — particularly the 'palm reading to palm trees' joke — is a voice-establishing comic aside that characterizes Miriam's dry observational humor. The draft collapses it into 'murals and lava-lamp dreams oozing down the street,' losing the joke entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the 'palm reading to palm trees' quip and one additional detail from the neighborhood description to preserve the narrator's sardonic register.

findings.source_passage: The old smell of the industrial, human world was wonderful to behold.
findings.source_locator: after Miriam sits in Heather's apartment, before Heather's 'you don't look like you've been kidnapped' line
findings.why_it_matters: This beat carries interpretive weight: Miriam's relief at being back in the human world underscores her ambivalence about the dragon world and sets up the tension of the chapter. Its absence flattens the emotional arc and removes the contrast that makes her eventual decision to return more meaningful.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a single sentence capturing Miriam's sensory relief at returning to the human/industrial world before Heather's observation about her appearance.

findings.source_passage: Heather let out a squeal as she plopped herself in the chair beside me.
findings.source_locator: during the argument about Miriam liking Xander, after 'He had me kidnapped so he could keep up some kind of—'
findings.why_it_matters: The squeal is a small but character-specific beat for Heather that the draft drops, slightly flattening the comic energy of the dialogue exchange.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert Heather's gleeful squeal or an equivalent physical reaction at the appropriate moment in the dialogue.

summary: The draft is largely faithful, preserving all major plot beats, most key dialogue, and the chapter's comic-romantic dynamic, but two medium-severity voice flattenings — loss of the 'palm reading to palm trees' joke and the 'industrial human world' sensory beat — thin the narrator's register without quite triggering regeneration.
